_comment: PLAT-35 — THE TIER-4 READINGS OF THE GPUI FRONT-END'S OWN FRAMES.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM `tier4-review.json`, SAID FIRST BECAUSE
THE SPLIT IS THE DECISION MOST LIKELY TO BE READ AS EVASION.
`tier4-review.json` is the gated deliverable: the suite refuses it four
ways and a reading scoring below 4 BLOCKS unless it is in that file's
`knownRed` block, which asserts in both directions that the quarantined
set is EXACTLY the set scoring below 4. RE-COUNTED 2026-10-03, because
this paragraph was written over twelve readings and there are now
TWENTY-FOUR: THIRTEEN OF TWENTY-FOUR score below 4 — six of six in
iteration 1, four of six in iteration 2, NONE in iteration 3 and three of
six in iteration 4. (Iteration 4's three are `shell`, `state` and
`eventLog`. They are not a regression and this file does not re-score an
earlier reading: each of the three named an already-open entry owned by
another milestone — F8, F3 and F5 — and the SAME frame drew a 6 from
iteration 3's reader and a 3 from iteration 4's. That spread between
readers is itself why the scores are not the gate.) Putting them in
`knownRed` would still mean quarantining thirteen entries, and a
quarantine ledger holding thirteen of twenty-four entries is not a
quarantine — it is the gate
switched off while wearing the shape of a gate. So the SCORES here are
ungated, the findings are carried in PLAT-35's status with
owners, and `tier4-review.json` is left exactly as it was: six readings of
the ELECTRON arm, with its two quarantines.
THE SCORES ARE UNGATED. THE FILE IS NOT (added 2026-10-02).
`src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` re-derives this
file's `gate` counts from its own `findings`, checks `gate.met` against
them in BOTH directions, requires a unique id, an owner, a closed-set
severity and substantial text on every finding, refuses a finding that is
both resolved and unresolved, and checks the reading population against
`scenarios.json` — count per iteration, each scenario once, and every
reading's view and viewport against that file's own tables. Until that
suite existed NOTHING in the tree read this file: `grep -rn` for its name
found it in prose only. An unread ledger's least reliable sentence is its
own summary, which is `Verification-Harness-Traps.md` 4; declining to gate
a SCORE is a decision, and leaving a record unread is not one.
WHAT THESE READINGS ARE OF. The frames of the GPUI front-end's own scene,
captured by `ci/test/plat35-gpui-capture.sh` through
`codetracer-gpui --pixels-out`. Before iteration 1 PLAT-35's GPUI arm was
the SHADOW TREE only (`PLAT35-VG1`), so no tier-4 reading of that
front-end existed to score.
THEY ARE AGENT READINGS, DECLARED AS SUCH, exactly as `tier4-review.json`
declares its six. There have been ZERO human reviews of the GPUI arm.
HOW TO READ THE RATINGS. The brief's own grammar makes below-4 a MISSING
OR DISTORTED ELEMENT rather than an aesthetic opinion. In iterations 1 and
2 every reading below 4 was there for one finding — the window drew no
debug-controls strip at all (`PLAT35-F1`). Iteration 3 is the first taken
AFTER upstream's chrome work and against the corpus's real 116-line
program, and `PLAT35-F1` is closed there, so iteration 3's numbers are not
comparable with iterations 1 and 2 as a trend: a different window, a
different recording and a different set of open findings.
THE GATE IS THE LEDGER AND NOT THE NUMBER. `findings` below is the
ledger; PLAT-35's status carries it with an owner per entry. After
iteration 4 SIX P1 and SIX P2 entries are unresolved (it closed
`PLAT35-F13` and `PLAT35-F14`), so the gate is NOT met and the milestone
stays `partial`.

gate.iteration4: TWO P2 ENTRIES CLOSED — `PLAT35-F13` and `PLAT35-F14`, both PLAT-35's own, both in `leaves.gutterText` — so the counts move from 6 P1 / 8 P2 to 6 P1 / 6 P2 and TWELVE remain. `met` is false either way. OF THE FIVE THIS MILESTONE OWNED, THREE REMAIN: `PLAT35-F3` (P1, and it is the GPUI twin of `PLAT35-PD1` — ellipsis versus scrollbar is one decision for both front-ends and it is being raised with the user, so it was deliberately not touched here), `PLAT35-F10` (blocked on the design system publishing a hex for `layout_questions.DesignTokenAlphabet`, which `chrome.nim`'s own header says it does not) and `PLAT35-F11` (blocked on PLAT-42's OCR lane being Wayland-only on this host, re-checked and still true). THE CLOSURES ARE NOT A SHORTCUT AND THE SUITE NO LONGER LETS THEM BE: the gap this note itself named — *'`resolved` entries are checked for nothing but id-disjointness, so moving an entry from `findings` to `resolved` is the one edit that lowers both counts and reddens nothing'* — was CLOSED in the same pass. `test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` now requires a closed-set severity, a text floor, a `remedy` and a `confirmedBy` on every resolved entry, which is six more checks per entry, and the two closures above carry structural readings at both viewports, two independent pixel readings, a census control, a tier-3 suite and a RED CONTROL RUN of that suite against the pre-fix code. A STATED COST, because it is not nothing: the gutter is one cell wider on every row, which makes `PLAT35-F3`'s clipping one column worse at both viewports. AND A STATED DEBT, found at the adversarial review of this iteration and measured rather than estimated. Editing `app/leaves.nim` and `gpui/chrome.nim` moves the `*-control.sha256` digests of SEVEN mutation harnesses, every one of which was GREEN at the parent commit `c05d8443a`. The counts the implementer wrote into those two files were both wrong and are corrected in them: SIX harnesses digest `leaves.nim` (plat20, plat22, plat35-visual, and — never previously noticed, because every earlier count read only `src/frontend/gpui/tests/` — plat42-surface, plat47-parity and plat49-chrome), not three; THREE digest `chrome.nim` (plat37-window, plat47-parity, plat49-chrome); and `plat38-input` does NOT digest `scenarios.json` — only plat35-visual and plat37-window do. ALL SEVEN WERE THEN RUN at the parent commit rather than argued about, because §39 forbids re-recording without re-grading but does not license leaving a lane red unexamined. ONE GRADES ON THIS HOST: `plat20` scored 14 of 14 KILLED, so it was re-graded against these bytes and ITS DIGEST IS RE-RECORDED IN THIS COMMIT. The other six refuse, each for a reason that is the host's and not this change's: `plat22` refuses for a missing `src/build-debug/bin/replay-server`, which would otherwise score every arm MIS-ATTRIBUTED; `plat47-parity` and `plat49-chrome` answer 'REFUSING TO RUN: REPLAY_SERVER_BIN is not exported', their needle scans passing at 0 problems; `plat35-visual` grades 0 of 9 KILLED with all nine DID-NOT-COMPILE — including its `.md` and `.json` subjects, which no mutation could have broken — because its suite reads `../codetracer-specs/Testing/Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md` and the sibling now keeps that file under `spec/Testing/`; `plat42-surface` aborts on a red baseline (`test_gpui_editing_surface.nim`, which needs `/proc/self/statm`); and `plat37-window` refuses for want of `build/plat37/manifest.json`, which only the Wayland-only windowed capture lane writes. gate.note: **THIS PARAGRAPH IS ITERATION 3's AND ITS COUNTS ARE ITERATION 3's; `iteration4` above carries the current ones (6 P1 / 6 P2 / twelve remaining).** It is kept rather than rewritten because it is the record of what the review decided on that date. A numeric rating is a summary of this ledger and not a substitute for it. Iteration 3 is a RE-GRADE at 73e8c3dc4 against the corpus's real 116-line program and it moved the ledger in both directions: two P1 entries (F1, F6) and the capture-provenance entry (C1) closed on upstream work and a real recording, F9 was rewritten to the residue of a finding whose three measured halves closed, F10 was re-characterised, F14 stopped being an arithmetic claim, and ONE NEW ENTRY was opened (F17). FOURTEEN remain. THE COUNTS, AND THE ONE THE REVIEW MOVED: the re-grade filed F17 at P2 and published five P1 / nine P2; the review raised F17 to P1 (see its `severityRaisedAtReview`) because it is the still-failing half of the expected-elements clause F1 was a P1 for, so the published counts are SIX P1 and EIGHT P2. The total is fourteen either way and `met` is false either way — P1 and P2 block this gate identically — but a P1 count that falls because one clause was split across two owners is not progress, and it is not recorded as any. THE FRAMING FINDING, stated here because it is about the milestone and not about a frame, RE-PARTITIONED at review because the first version of this sentence added to fourteen while mis-sorting one entry: of the fourteen, FIVE are PLAT-35's to fix — F3 (jointly with PLAT35-PD1), F10, F11 (jointly with PLAT-42's OCR grammar, and blocked on a Wayland-only lane), F13, F14 — TWO are explicitly NOT GPUI-side (F8 is PLAT-45's, F17 is the shared mark set's and the design system's), and the remaining SEVEN are owned by PLAT-40 (F2, F4, F7), PLAT-41 (F5, F12), PLAT-47/PLAT-40 (F9) and PLAT-21/PLAT-3 (VG8). Of the six P1s, FIVE are not PLAT-35's to fix (F2, F4, F5, F7 and F17) and one is (F3). A gate worded as 'zero unresolved P1 and P2' over a ledger whose majority is other milestones' work is not reachable within PLAT-35 alone. These numbers are not only prose: `src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` RE-DERIVES unresolvedP1 and unresolvedP2 from `findings` and checks `met` against them in both directions, so a count that drifts from its own ledger is a failing case rather than a sentence nobody reads. WHAT THAT SUITE DID NOT GATE, found at this review and CLOSED IN ITERATION 4: it checked the shape of the UNRESOLVED set only. `resolved` entries were checked for nothing but id-disjointness — no closed-set severity, no text floor, no evidence — so moving an entry from `findings` to `resolved` was the one edit that lowers both counts and reddens nothing. That is why F1 and F6 were re-measured here by hand rather than taken on the ledger's word, and iteration 4 — the first pass that actually moves an entry across — made the hand-check a case: a resolved entry now needs a closed-set severity, substantial text, a `remedy` and a `confirmedBy`. An `owner` is still not required of a closed entry, and that is stated in the suite.
